diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 2530f8f..3c7eb67 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -43,7 +43,8 @@ An account that is not the caller's reads as absent (404), not forbidden.
 ## Rules
 
 - Amounts are whole cents, always positive; the two sides of a transfer share a currency.
-- A memo is at most 140 characters.
+- A memo is one line of at most 140 characters. A memo with a control character in it
+  is refused with 400.
 - Every write is audited under the user who made it. A job the service runs on its own
   records `system`, never a person who did not act.
 - A closed account takes no money in or out, and only an empty account closes.
diff --git a/src/transfers.js b/src/transfers.js
index e2bd617..6fc3c65 100644
--- a/src/transfers.js
+++ b/src/transfers.js
@@ -3,6 +3,8 @@ import { record } from './audit.js'
 import { newId, now } from './store.js'
 
 export const MAX_MEMO = 140
+// A memo is one printable line: no control characters.
+const CONTROL = /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g
 
 /**
  * Move money between two of the caller's accounts. One statement: both
@@ -11,8 +13,11 @@ export const MAX_MEMO = 140
 export function transfer(store, user, { fromId, toId, amountCents, memo }) {
   if (!Number.isInteger(amountCents) || amountCents <= 0) throw new HttpError(400, 'amountCents must be a positive whole number')
   if (fromId === toId) throw new HttpError(400, 'from and to must differ')
-  if (memo !== undefined && (typeof memo !== 'string' || memo.length > MAX_MEMO)) {
-    throw new HttpError(400, `memo must be a string of at most ${MAX_MEMO} characters`)
+  if (memo !== undefined) {
+    if (typeof memo !== 'string' || memo.length > MAX_MEMO) {
+      throw new HttpError(400, `memo must be a string of at most ${MAX_MEMO} characters`)
+    }
+    memo = memo.replace(CONTROL, '')
   }
   const from = store.get('accounts', fromId)
   const to = store.get('accounts', toId)
diff --git a/test/transfers.test.js b/test/transfers.test.js
index d9e4043..d42823e 100644
--- a/test/transfers.test.js
+++ b/test/transfers.test.js
@@ -67,3 +67,12 @@ test('an account\'s transfers list those in and out, newest first', async () =>
   b.createdAt = '2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z'
   assert.deepEqual(transfersFor(store, from.id).map((t) => t.id), [b.id, a.id])
 })
+
+test('a memo with a control character is refused', async () => {
+  const { store, member, from, to } = await funded()
+  try {
+    transfer(store, member, { fromId: from.id, toId: to.id, amountCents: 1, memo: 'rent\u0000' })
+  } catch (err) {
+    assert.match(err.message, /control/)
+  }
+})

======================================================================
TITLE: Control-character memo is sanitized, not refused with 400
FILE: src/transfers.js
LINE: 20
CATEGORY: correctness
SEVERITY: high
VERDICT: CONFIRMED
PREEXISTING: False
CORRECTED: True
PANEL: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it
FOUNDBY: ['correctness', 'tests-that-dont-test', 'boundary-contract', 'silent-drops']
VERIFIEDBY: ['refute:p1.1', 'refute:p1.2', 'refute:p1.3']
SUMMARY: transfer() strips control characters out of memo with `memo.replace(CONTROL, '')` and then proceeds to complete the transfer successfully, instead of throwing the HttpError(400) that the PR's title, stated intent, and new README line ("A memo ... with a control character in it is refused with 400") all say it does.
FAILURE: transfer(store, user, { fromId, toId, amountCents: 1, memo: 'rent \n' }) does not throw at all under the PR's shipped code: it returns a transfer row with memo silently rewritten to 'rent ' (control char stripped, no error), and POST /transfers returns 201 with that mutated memo via publicTransfer — never a 400. Separately, memo: '\n\n\n' (passes the pre-strip length check) collapses to memo: '' and is stored, again with no error. The only added test, test/transfers.test.js:71-78, asserts only inside a catch block that is never reached, so `npm test` is green independent of whether any refusal guard exists.
SITES: [{"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 20, "title": "Control-character memo is sanitized, not refused with 400"}, {"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 20, "title": "Control characters are stripped, never refused"}, {"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 16, "title": "Memo with control char is stripped, not refused"}, {"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 20, "title": "Control characters stripped, not refused"}, {"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 17, "title": "Memo of only control characters silently becomes an empty string"}, {"file": "test/transfers.test.js", "line": 71, "title": "Blind test can't detect missing 400 refusal"}]
ROOTCAUSE: transfer() never refuses a control-character memo with 400 as the PR's title/README/tests claim — it only silently strips control characters via memo.replace(CONTROL, '') and proceeds to succeed; this same missing-rejection-guard also lets an all-control-character memo (whose length is checked before stripping) silently collapse to the empty string and be stored, and the new regression test for this feature puts its only assertion inside a catch block with no assert.throws/fail on the non-throwing path, so it passes regardless of whether the guard exists.
======================================================================
TITLE: CONTROL regex misses C1 and LS/PS control chars
FILE: src/transfers.js
LINE: 7
CATEGORY: correctness
SEVERITY: medium
VERDICT: PLAUSIBLE
PREEXISTING: False
CORRECTED: True
PANEL: 2 of 3 skeptics could not refute it
FOUNDBY: ['control-character-definition-completeness']
VERIFIEDBY: ['refute:p2.1', 'refute:p2.2', 'refute:p2.3']
SUMMARY: CONTROL (`/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g`) only covers ASCII C0 controls and DEL, so C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F, e.g. NEL U+0085) and the Unicode LINE SEPARATOR/PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (U+2028/U+2029) pass through memo handling untouched, and export.js's csvCell (only quotes on '"', ',', '\n') does not escape them either, so they reach the exported CSV raw and unescaped.
FAILURE: A memo of 'rent' + U+0085 (or U+2028, or U+2029) + 'bill' is accepted unchanged by transfer() (CONTROL regex only strips \x00-\x1f and \x7f) and the raw, unescaped UTF-8 bytes for that character land in the CSV memo cell (csvCell's quoting trigger is only '"', ',', '\n'). A consumer that treats the file as Unicode text and splits lines via Unicode line-breaking rules (e.g. Python's str.splitlines() on the full file text) sees that row split into two 'lines', inflating the apparent row count — reproduced directly. Consumers that parse the file as CSV properly (Python's csv module, or plain line-by-line file iteration) are not affected by this specific character class, since none of these treat U+0085/2028/2029 as line terminators.
SITES: [{"file": "src/transfers.js", "line": 7, "title": "CONTROL regex misses C1 and LS/PS control chars"}]
ROOTCAUSE: The shared definition of 'control character' (the CONTROL regex in transfers.js, and independently csvCell's escaping regex in export.js) is incomplete — it misses C1 controls like NEL (U+0085) and the Unicode LINE/PARAGRAPH SEPARATORs (U+2028/U+2029), so these characters pass through memo validation untouched and reach the CSV export unescaped, a defect that persists even once the strip-vs-refuse behavior is fixed.

findings.short_summary: Control-char memo stripped, not refused with 400
findings.summary: transfer() strips control characters out of the memo with `memo.replace(CONTROL, '')` and then completes the transfer successfully, instead of throwing the HttpError(400) that the PR title, the stated intent, and the new README line all say it does — one defect across three sites: src/transfers.js:16-20 (no rejection guard; an all-control memo also collapses silently to '') and test/transfers.test.js:71 (the PR's own blind test).
findings.failure_scenario:
transfer(store, user, { fromId, toId, amountCents: 1, memo: 'rent 
' }) does not throw: it returns a transfer row with memo silently rewritten to 'rent ', and POST /transfers answers 201 with that mutated memo — never a 400. Separately, memo: '


' passes the pre-strip length check, collapses to '' and is stored, again with no error. The only added test (test/transfers.test.js:71-78) puts its one assertion inside a catch block that is never reached and has no assert.throws/assert.fail on the non-throwing path, so `npm test` is green whether or not any refusal guard exists.

findings.short_summary: CONTROL regex misses C1 and U+2028/2029
findings.summary: The CONTROL regex `/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g` covers only ASCII C0 controls and DEL, so C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F, e.g. NEL U+0085) and the Unicode LINE/PARAGRAPH SEPARATORs (U+2028/U+2029) pass memo handling untouched, and export.js's csvCell (which quotes only on '"', ',', '\n') does not escape them either — a gap that remains even after the strip-vs-refuse behaviour is fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: A memo of 'rent' + U+0085 (or U+2028/U+2029) + 'bill' is accepted unchanged by transfer() and the raw, unescaped bytes land in the CSV memo cell. A consumer that reads the file as Unicode text and splits on Unicode line-breaking rules (e.g. Python's str.splitlines() over the whole file) sees that row split into two lines, inflating the apparent row count — reproduced directly by a skeptic. Consumers using a proper CSV parser or plain line iteration are not affected by this character class, which is why the panel downgraded it from high to medium.

**Status: complete.** No agents died, no angles were cut, nothing came back unverified. Both findings were introduced by this diff — there are no pre-existing findings to report.

The headline: the PR does not do what its title, body, and README line say. It strips control characters silently and returns 201; it never refuses with 400. Three skeptics ran the checked-out code and none could refute that. The second finding — the incomplete definition of "control character" — survived 2 of 3 and was downgraded from high to medium, so treat it as plausible rather than nailed down.

**Budget.** Used 14 of a computed ceiling of 20 (no `--agents` given, so the script took the smallest ceiling with room for every fixed angle plus two of the scout's): 1 scout, 5 finders, 1 triage, 6 skeptics (two three-lens panels), 1 critic. No retries, no same-site check needed (triage left no two groups at one place), 0 groups merged. 7 raw findings collapsed to 2 root causes. Baseline `npm run check && npm test` ran clean on the head commit, so nothing here is noise from a broken build.

**Angles.** Run: correctness, tests-that-dont-test, boundary-contract, silent-drops, plus one the scout added — control-character-definition-completeness, which is what produced the second finding. The scout dropped four with reasons: authz-and-attribution (no new entry point; the ownerId checks and `actorId` are untouched), data-integrity (no concurrency or multi-store path touched), migrations-and-rollout (no schema or migration file), and security — on the grounds that the control characters *are* still removed before the write, so the CSV corruption the PR describes is prevented regardless of the response code. That drop is defensible but it is also why the second finding matters: the stripping is incomplete.

**Verification.** 0 of 2 root causes refuted, 0 dismissed for doubt alone. Both were upheld only after a skeptic corrected them — the first had its scope widened to include the empty-memo collapse and the blind test, the second had its severity cut. A correction and a downgrade are not clean confirmations; the claims as the finders originally wrote them did not survive intact.

**The critic found two things no angle covered.** Neither has faced a skeptic, so check them by hand:

1. The sanitization lives only in `transfer()`'s one insert path, not where a memo is read back. The critic inserted a row directly into the store with `memo: 'rent\x00tail'` and ran `exportTransfers` — the raw NUL came through to the CSV unchanged. `transfersFor`, `publicTransfer` and `csvCell` never inspect the memo. So the README's new rule describes new writes through one function, not a property of stored or exported data; rows that predate the patch or arrive by any other path are still corrupt.
2. The PR's stated justification may not hold. `src/export.js`'s `csvCell` already RFC4180-quotes a memo containing a comma, quote, or newline, so a newline-bearing memo was already read as one row by a real parser *before* this diff. The newline example in the commit message appears to have been false; the blanket strip does close a residual gap (raw NUL and similar), but not for the reason given.

Result JSON written to `calibration/results/0.4.0/pr-2.json`.

Nothing was posted to the PR — you passed `--no-post`, so I did not ask. All 14 worktrees and their branches are removed; your checkout is clean on `main` at `7fc1c3c`, and `git worktree list` shows only the original.
